`JSON.parse(text) as User` tells the type checker what the data is, and checks nothing. Under [`bun build --compile --aot`](/bundler/aot-types#data-from-outside-keeps-its-shape) nothing checks it either. Data that lacks `name`, or whose `id` is a string, goes on as it is, as in plain JavaScript.

The price is speed. The compiler can no longer rely on the shape of a `User`, of the types inside it, or of the types its values are assigned to. It looks their properties up by name, or checks them when the program runs, everywhere in your program.

This rule lists the places where such data enters your program: an `as` on a value of type `any` or `unknown` that comes from `JSON.parse()`, from a function or a package without types, from a `catch` clause, or from a variable declared `any` or `unknown`. There are usually few of them, and they are the places to validate.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. This rule needs types, so turning it on makes `bun lint` type check your code first.

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"bun/aot-outside-data" = "error" # or "warn"
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 2} */}
```ts
interface User {
  id: number;
  name: string;
}

declare const text: string;
const user = JSON.parse(text) as User;

function messageOf(error: unknown): string {
  return (error as Error).message;
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```ts
interface Animal {
  name: string;
}
interface Dog extends Animal {
  bark(): void;
}

function walk(animal: Animal) {
  (animal as Dog).bark();
}
```

That cast starts from a value that has a type.

Validate, and the cast is not needed:

{/* good */}
```ts
function messageOf(error: unknown): string {
  return error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
}
```

## How it relates to `no-unsafe-type-assertion`

[`@typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-type-assertion`](/lint/rules/typescript/no-unsafe-type-assertion) reports every cast that narrows a type, such as `animal as Dog`. This rule reports only the casts of data that has no type at all. Where both are on, that rule leaves these casts to this one, unless it is an error and this one is a warning: then you see both.
